newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissho Iwai in $3.1 bln Indonesian petchem project.
newsitem.headline: Nissho Iwai in $3.1 bln Indonesian petchem project.

text.p: Japanese trading house Nissho Iwai Corp said on Friday that it would sign a $3.1 billion project on Friday to build a petrochemical complex in Indonesia.
The contract will be signed with an Indonesian industrial group headed by P.T. Tirtamas Majutama and a Thai industrial group headed by Siam Cement Co Plc.
U.S. petrochemical firm Koch Industries Inc is also considering participating in the project, Nissho Iwai said.

The planned three million tonnes of output of oil products and basic petrochemical products will include 700,000 tonnes of ethylene, 500,000 tonnes of paraxylene and 380,000 tonnes of propylene, Nissho Iwai said.

In the future, the complex is also expected to make 500,000 tonnes of styrene monomer a year, as well as 300,000 tonnes of low density polyethylene, 200,000 tonnes of polypropylene and 180,000 tonnes of high density polyethylene, the company said.
